reports.title: CoreWeave Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Results

guidance.heading: Business Outlook
section: We are raising our full year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $13.0 billion to $13.3 billion.

We are also raising our full year 2026 adjusted operating income2 guidance to a range of $1.275 billion to $1.375 billion, representing a 26% increase at the midpoint compared with our prior guidance.
We continue to expect more than 1.85 gigawatts of active power at year-end.

We now expect full year 2026 capital expenditures of $37 billion to $39 billion, raising the low end of our prior guidance range of $35 billion to $39 billion. This is as a result of our expectation to deploy infrastructure and deliver it to customers sooner than planned.
We expect interest expense for Q4 2026 in the range of $1.05 to $1.15 billion.
Finally, we are raising our annualized run-rate revenue3 guidance to $20 billion to $21 billion to exit 2026.

desk.headline: Revenue up 168% to $3.66bn, beat; full-year revenue and profit outlook raised above estimates
results: Sales jumped 168% to $3.66bn, more than $1bn higher than the June quarter and above the company's own $3.45–3.60bn range.
Adjusted operating margin reached 10%, but interest costs of $846m left a net loss of $709m ($1.27 a share).
Backlog of contracted work rose to about $132.5bn; active power passed 1.7 GW and contracted power 4.6 GW.
Operating cash flow was $1.98bn, while spending on equipment and data centres was $9.4bn in the quarter.
Raised about $4.2bn in convertible notes, closed a $2.6bn loan and set up a share-sale programme for up to 35m shares.

guidance.summary: CoreWeave raised its 2026 revenue and adjusted operating income ranges and lifted the bottom of its capex range; it expects to exit 2026 at a $20–21bn annual revenue run-rate.

points: The CFO said there are no plans for more parent-level unsecured debt through 2027 at today's yields, with under $5bn of new parent debt expected over that time.
About $9bn of customer prepayments and deposits is expected in the next three months, helping fund the build-out.
The CEO said almost all contracted power is already online or permitted and under construction.
Management said margins hit double digits a quarter early; the CEO told Bloomberg he sees positive net income in 2028.
The CEO said he expects no impact from US political moves against data centres and no change in the Nvidia partnership.
call.source: Call coverage: The Next Web, 11 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Whether interest costs (guided at $1.05–1.15bn for Q4) keep running ahead of adjusted operating income.
Delivery of new capacity on time to reach more than 1.85 GW of active power by year-end.
How the new customer-backed loan and share-sale programme affect debt and dilution.
